reason: B's format pads with zeros on the wrong (least-significant) side when min_digits exceeds the natural length (e.g. 12345 with min 7 gives 1234500), while A pads correctly on the left and is otherwise equivalent.

A and B validate the port before the host, violating the R3 host-then-port order (e.g. an empty or invalid host followed by a bad port returns InvalidPort), while C (like D) validates host first and otherwise matches the spec.

A validates every segment before rejecting a trailing slash (so /%GG/ reports 1), handles wildcard placement, ranking and tie-breaking correctly, whereas D returns the trailing-slash error before validating preceding segments.

B only protects a quote at raw byte 0 (not the first retained byte after leading CFWS) and its CFWS boundary check treats any run as legal whenever an @ exists, so it never reports CfwsBoundary for CFWS inside the local or domain; A implements both correctly.
A accepts the tile value 1 as valid (1 is a power of two but outside 2..=2^31), while D correctly rejects it and implements moves, merges, overflow and legality per spec.
A emits no byte for an xx== group and B reports a pending position-two = at EOF using a stale offset, while C decodes xx== correctly and reports the = offset itself.

A never emits the n-1 empty strings for paragraph boundaries (its empty placeholder segments are skipped) and compares hyphenation cost against (C-len-1)^2 instead of (C-len)^2, while B handles both correctly.

B prints all simultaneous end lines with the same post-release snapshot and C emits simultaneous ends in descending ID and loses worker cooldowns after completion (and can panic), whereas A emits each end in ascending ID with its own snapshot and tracks cooldowns.
